drills.label: Cold open
drills.question_line: SAM: A hospital group's platform team wrote a procedure that checks code changes for patient data leaking
drills.answer_line: SAM: It does. So, B. A plugin gives group targeting
drills.scenario: Hospital procedure shared across six teams
drills.stem: A platform team's procedure checks code changes for patient data leaking into logs. Six product teams must run it the same way. Last month a bad shared prompt edit hit every team for a week before anyone could undo it. How should the procedure reach the teams?

options.A: Upload it as an org-provisioned Skill under Organization settings
options.B: Plugin assigned to all six teams' groups, version-controlled updates from a repo, a named owner
options.C: Copy it as a project Skill into each team's repository
options.D: Add a paragraph describing it to each team's CLAUDE.md

drills.why: "Could not undo it" plus "a named owner" means governance decides. Org-provisioned Skills have no version pinning or native rollback; a plugin gives a path back.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. A retail bank's internal coding assistant has slowed noticeably
drills.stem: A bank's internal coding assistant has slowed noticeably over three weeks. Nothing was deployed; the team recently pointed it at a much larger document set. What should the architect do first?

options.A: Switch to a smaller, faster model
options.B: Use request traces to find the slowest span: tokens per request, slowest tool call, cache behaviour
options.C: Raise client timeouts so requests stop failing
options.D: Roll back to the previous release and re-run integration tests

drills.why: "First" with nothing diagnosed means gather evidence. Latency maps to context growth, a slow tool or a cache miss; the larger document set points at context.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. Choose two. A field-service company gave three hundred engineers
drills.stem: 300 engineers got Claude Code two months ago. Usage sits with a handful of people, and last week a generated change merged that its author could not explain. Which two actions address the root causes?

options.A: A champion in each team converts a real workflow, then seeds adoption in batches
options.B: Verification checklist: correctness, security, maintainability, human understanding, automated where possible
options.C: Exempt changes under 50 lines from security review to keep queues moving
options.D: Default every session to the most capable model for strong first impressions
options.E: Let each engineer build their own configuration to suit personal style

drills.why: A fixes lumpy adoption; B adds the missing understanding gate. C widens the gap, D ignores spend posture, E is the drift a shared baseline prevents.

drills.question_line: SAM: Before the recap, pause and name the three task statements from today, and one mechanism that belongs to each. [pause]
drills.answer_line: ALEX: Configuring tools for teams, with a plugin for governed Skills.
drills.prompt: Name the three task statements from today, and one mechanism that belongs to each.
drills.answer: Configuring tools for teams: a plugin for governed Skills. Improving developer workflows: the verification checklist. Debugging and operational support: a runbook and an escalation path.
